claims.text: A Pulumi blog post titled 'SST Runs on the Pulumi Engine: What It Means to Build on Pulumi' exists at /blog/sst-built-on-pulumi/.
The post at /blog/sst-built-on-pulumi/ covers the engine mechanics behind SST's migration from CDK to Pulumi.
AWS CDK ties infrastructure to AWS only and multi-cloud is nearly impossible with it.
AWS CDK supports defining infrastructure only in TypeScript or Python.
Pulumi supports any programming language; Pulumi supports TypeScript, Python, Go, or C#.
Pulumi supports AWS, Azure, GCP, and on-prem infrastructure.
Pulumi deployments are faster than AWS CDK due to direct execution, while CDK is slower due to CloudFormation.
AWS CDK secrets management is limited to AWS Secrets Manager only, whereas Pulumi supports cross-cloud secrets.
With AWS CDK state is a CloudFormation state file, whereas Pulumi state is Pulumi-managed.
CDK and CloudFormation act as a code generator producing an intermediary format (YAML or JSON) that is then executed to deploy resources.
Pulumi does not generate an intermediary format; infrastructure code is executed directly during deployment.

A Founding Engineer at SST said: 'With Pulumi, the deployment process feels like a natural extension of writing code - it's intuitive and powerful and capable of advanced things that traditional IaC tools can't handle.'
Pulumi has built-in extensibility features such as custom providers and dynamic components.
Pulumi Insights product page describes improved visibility and debugging capabilities.
Ion is the code name for a new engine for deploying SST applications, deploying components using Pulumi instead of CDK and CloudFormation; once stable it will be released as SST v3.
SST uses Pulumi behind the scenes for its providers and deployment engine and bridges Terraform providers through Pulumi.
SST makes money primarily through its managed service SST Console, which is optional and includes a free tier.
Pulumi Crosswalk for AWS simplifies 'day one' tasks, documented in the AWS guide at /docs/iac/guides/clouds/aws/.
In its early days SST was built on top of AWS CDK.
Pulumi lets SST offer a faster, more flexible, and provider-agnostic infrastructure experience.
SST v3 replaced AWS CDK and CloudFormation with an embedded Pulumi engine that calls Terraform-bridged providers to make cloud API calls.
Running `sst deploy` requires no separate Pulumi install and no Pulumi account or Pulumi Cloud; the Pulumi engine ships inside the SST CLI.
SST keeps its state in an S3 bucket in the user's own AWS account rather than in Pulumi Cloud.
SST is an open source TypeScript framework from the team formerly known as Serverless Stack, for deploying to AWS and more than 150 other providers.
SST apps are defined in a single `sst.config.ts` file using SST components.
Through 2023 SST's provisioning layer was built on AWS CDK and CloudFormation; in late 2023 the team began a rewrite code-named Ion.
Ion shipped as SST v3 in mid-2024 and has been the only supported architecture since.

SST's blog post 'Moving away from CDK' says: "Ion is a code name for a new engine for deploying SST applications. The constructs (or components) are defined using Terraform providers and deployed using Pulumi; as opposed to CDK and CloudFormation (CFN)."

SST's blog post 'Moving away from CDK' says: "When you run `sst deploy`, those resources make a call to an embedded Pulumi engine that makes a call to their bridged Terraform provider, and this makes the AWS SDK calls to create your resources."
SST docs 'What is SST' say: "SST uses Pulumi behind the scenes for the providers and the deployment engine. And Terraform's providers are bridged through Pulumi."
Gautier Blandin's article says SST uses the Pulumi engine under the hood and lets users write Pulumi code in addition to SST constructs.
Kiryl Anoshka's dev.to article says: "You may notice right away the imports from Pulumi. It means the whole deployment process will be built on Pulumi now."
SST's platform package.json depends on @pulumi/pulumi, first-party Pulumi providers for AWS, Cloudflare, Docker builds, and more, plus the @pulumiverse/vercel provider.
The SST repository is anomalyco/sst (formerly sst/sst).
The Pulumi engine diffs desired vs actual state, builds a dependency graph, and orders operations.
Pulumi's Terraform bridge is Apache-2.0 licensed.
Pulumi's engine does not require a Pulumi account, a network call to Pulumi Cloud, or any Pulumi-hosted service to run.
Pulumi's Automation API lets teams embed Pulumi programs inside their own tools, and the provider bridge lets Pulumi users consume Terraform providers directly.
AWS alone exposes hundreds of resource types.
Nitric's docs state "all of the direct deployment providers use Pulumi under the hood for their deployments," with official Nitric providers built on Pulumi's AWS, GCP, and Azure providers.
Defang's Pulumi provider takes a Compose file, translates it to a Pulumi program, and runs `pulumi up`; Defang deploys Docker Compose applications to the cloud.
Resources without a dedicated SST construct can be defined directly with Pulumi and deployed as part of the same SST app.
SST doesn't invoke the Terraform CLI or write Terraform state.
The latest SST release, v4.17.1, went out in July 2026.
The `sst` npm package gets roughly 796,000 downloads a week (796,291 for September 5-11, 2026).
SST's team page credits the same team behind opencode, an open source AI coding agent.
opencode has a larger following on GitHub than SST itself.
The team's broadened attention to opencode hasn't changed SST's release cadence or its dependency on the Pulumi engine.
Pulumi offers Pulumi Cloud, policy as code, and components for sharing infrastructure patterns across an organization.
SST is a strong fit for an opinionated full-stack application framework, while Pulumi directly suits needs like cross-team visibility and policy enforcement.
Pulumi's Terraform bridge was built specifically to let projects like SST reuse Terraform's provider ecosystem.
